items.title: Jason Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2025
items.q: I’ve been playing with a tenor player, Mark Turner — I’ve been in his band for about ten years now

ctx.x: Do you find that there’s been occasions where you play less, a bit less, because you’re working with such wonderful — a wonderful rhythm section?

Yeah. Yup. Um hum. You know I’ve been playing with a tenor player, Mark Turner — I’ve been in his band for about ten years now, a little over ten years, going on eleven now I think. And we’ve done some clinics together at certain schools and everything. And he did this one exercise that I learned a lot from where he brought a horn player up and there was a rhythm section accompanying. And so they all played a tune. But he told the saxophone player he said, “Okay so when the tune starts I don’t want you to play…

horn players, they’ll get up and they want to just play their stuff and have other people follow them. Whereas he said, “Okay I want you to listen. Maybe listen to the drummer’s snare. Or maybe listen to the piano player’s left hand, you know what kind of rhythm they’re playing. Or maybe the bass player’s playing a certain harmonic or something you know.” And so I said wow, that’s a really cool way to go in to a solo when you’re improvising, just to say okay I’m going to be influenced by what I hear around me,…
